title: An Incremental Approach to Compiler Construction
why: The canonical step-by-step build of a tiny compiler that emits real x86-64 assembly from the simplest expressions upward, ideal for the first hands-on chapter.

title: System V Application Binary Interface: AMD64 Architecture Processor Supplement
why: The authoritative definition of x86-64 registers, stack frames, and the calling convention a code generator must follow on Linux.

title: Programming Techniques: Regular Expression Search Algorithm
why: Thompson's original construction turning a regular expression into an NFA, the theoretical basis of every regex-based lexer generator.

title: Regular Expression Matching Can Be Simple And Fast
why: A working engineer's readable walkthrough of Thompson NFA simulation versus backtracking, with runnable implementations.

title: Package go/scanner
why: Official documentation for a real hand-written production scanner, the concrete counterexample to generated lexers.

title: Top Down Operator Precedence
why: Pratt's original precedence-parsing method, the foundation of the expression parsers most production compilers use today.

title: Engineering a Compiler
why: A modern engineering-oriented textbook covering the full pipeline and, relevant here, context-free grammars, top-down and bottom-up parsing, and semantic analysis.

title: rust-analyzer syntax trees (docs/dev/syntax.md)
why: Describes a lossless, error-resilient syntax tree design in production tooling, the concrete model for the AST chapter.
